Part 2 · · Physical AI · 1 / 10

Physical AI: the agent gets a body

NVIDIA's definition: "Physical AI lets autonomous systems like cameras, robots, and self-driving cars perceive, understand, reason, perform or orchestrate complex actions in the physical world."

  • A software agent reads and writes text. A physical agent reads sensors and writes motor commands; the world grades the answer.
  • Three forces: models learned to act (VLAs), simulation made training cheap, agent SDKs made the model a planner that calls tools.
  • Jensen Huang, CES 2025: "the ChatGPT moment for general robotics is just around the corner."
Jul 2023 · models learn to actRT-2: Google DeepMind's vision-language-action model
Oct 2024 · models learn to actπ0: Physical Intelligence's robot foundation model
Jan 2025 · simulationCES: NVIDIA Cosmos world foundation models
Mar 2025 · simulationGR00T N1: NVIDIA's open humanoid foundation model
May 2025 · agentsStrands Agents SDK open-sourced by AWS
three forces, five dated events; each date's primary source is in the notes
Definition is a direct quote from NVIDIA's glossary page on physical AI (one sentence). The three forces are my framing; each is backed by a dated primary source on the timeline (DeepMind RT-2 blog 28 Jul 2023, "a novel vision-language-action (VLA) model"; Physical Intelligence pi0 blog 31 Oct 2024; NVIDIA GR00T N1 press release 18 Mar 2025, "the world's first open, fully customizable foundation model for generalized humanoid reasoning and skills", Newton "under development with Google DeepMind and Disney Research"; AWS Open Source blog "Introducing Strands Agents" 16 May 2025). The Huang line: Fortune, 8 Jan 2025, reporting the CES keynote of 6 Jan 2025; NVIDIA's own Cosmos press release of the same day quotes him as "The ChatGPT moment for robotics is coming." Say: this talk is about the third force, the agent SDK, applied to a car.
Part 2 · · strands-robots · 3 / 10

strands-robots: "control, simulate, and train robots with natural language"

The repo's own line: "Control robots and physical hardware with natural language through Strands Agents." One Robot() call: a MuJoCo simulation by default, a real robot with mode="real"; same code, same tool surface.

  • Control: the robot object is itself a Strands AgentTool; Agent(tools=[robot])("pick up the red cube").
  • Simulate: MuJoCo, Newton, Isaac and mjlab behind one SimEngine.
  • Train: LeRobot, Cosmos 3, PPO / FastSAC / FastTD3, Isaac Lab, SageMaker behind one create_trainer().
  • Mesh: every Robot(mesh=True) is a Zenoh peer; one fleet-wide e-stop.

Part 2 · · strands-robots · 4 / 10

The core loop: a tool call does not reach a motor without passing the gate

1 PROMPT"drive forward one metre"
→
2 AGENTStrands Agent picks a tool and an action
→
3 COMMAND GATEgate_motion: allowlist → bypass → refuse → ask
→
4 TRANSPORTserial, DDS, rosbridge, Zenoh mesh
→
5 ROBOTsim twin or metal; envelope comes back
← observation: {"status", "content": [text | json | image]} ←

Interventions

The gate raises a Strands interrupt, <tool>-command-approval. Only y / yes / approve / approved proceeds; the model never sees the reply. Reads and stops are never gated.

Headless runs

STRANDS_ROS2_COMMAND_ALLOW=/cmd_vel pre-approves one surface; BYPASS_TOOL_CONSENT=true allows all, with a WARNING. Nobody to ask: the call fails closed.

Audit

One JSONL row per verdict in ~/.strands_robots/mesh_audit.jsonl, HMAC-signed when STRANDS_MESH_AUDIT_PSK is set.

Physics stops the car; the decider explains.

Order of the gate is from docs/learn/agents.md "The operator gate": 1 allowlist variable names the command, allow silently; 2 BYPASS_TOOL_CONSENT=true, allow with a WARNING; 3 no tool_context, refuse naming the variable; 4 raise the interrupt named <tool>-command-approval; "y, yes, approve or approved proceeds, anything else declines; the model never sees the reply" (same page). Reads never gated: docs/learn/ros2.md; stop ungated: docs/start/first-agent.md ("Six read or halt, ungated"). The blocklist is matched on the final path segment, so /cmd_vel covers every namespace, and /manual_drive, /vehicle_state, /enable_state cover the DeepRacer. Audit path and HMAC from docs/learn/agents.md "Audit". Envelope shape from docs/start/first-robot.md. Say the safety line out loud: the gate is an explanation layer, not the safety layer; the pen, the hop cap and the marshal's thumb stop the car.

Part 2 · · strands-robots · 7 / 10

Train: record, verify, label, train, run it back

  • One contract: create_trainer(name).validate(spec) → train → status → export; validate launches nothing.
  • list_trainers() at main: cosmos3, fast_sac, fast_td3, isaaclab, lerobot_local, mock, ppo, sagemaker.
  • Imitation: LeRobot (ACT, Diffusion, SmolVLA, π0, GR00T N1.7) in-process; Cosmos 3 SFT; the same spec as one SageMaker job.
  • RL from a reward: SimEnv over any SimEngine; PPO, FastSAC, FastTD3; GPU-parallel via Isaac Lab.
  • Then create_policy("rl", checkpoint_dir=...) runs the checkpoint in the sim and, behind the gate, on the robot.

Part 3 · Why it fits a robot

Four things a robot needs, already in the SDK

  • Interventions. Typed decisions before each tool call, evaluated in order.
  • Hooks. BeforeToolCallEvent, AfterToolCallEvent, BeforeModelCallEvent: observe or change the loop at any point.
  • The command gate. strands-robots' _command_gate owns approval for every motion topic: a human "yes", or an explicit STRANDS_ROS2_COMMAND_ALLOW for headless runs.
  • Bidi voice with barge-in. BidiAgent keeps one connection to Nova Sonic; BidiBargeInEvent clears playback when the user talks over it.
tool call drive_deepracer(throttle=0.3, steer=-0.5)
before_tool_call: every handler votes, in order
PROCEEDAllow the operation to continue unchanged
GUIDECancel and provide feedback for the model to retry with
CONFIRMPause for human approval (before_tool_call only)
DENYBlock the operation; short-circuits remaining handlers
Physics stops the car; the decider explains.

Say the safety line out loud here, first time in this section: physics stops the car; the decider explains. Interventions are an explanation layer we can trust to be well behaved (fail-closed with on_error="deny"), not the thing that keeps a wheel off a foot. A fifth action, Transform, modifies event content in place; it is not on the slide.

The four descriptions are the interventions page's action table, word for word ("Allow the operation to continue unchanged", "Block the operation. Short-circuits remaining handlers", "Cancel and provide feedback for the model to retry with", "Pause for human approval"); the "before_tool_call only" qualifier is from the page's lifecycle table, and Confirm uses the SDK's interrupt/resume. The command gate description is from our code deep-dive of strands-robots (report 01, section 1.4). Barge-in: the bidi overview says the user can "talk over the agent (barge in)"; the stream-events page says to clear buffered audio when BidiBargeInEvent arrives, which AudioIO.output() does automatically.

Part 4 · Decision models

System 1 answers. System 2 writes.

  • A decision model picks between options or rates on a scale. It never writes free text.
  • Three typed answers, one forward pass: noul (yes/no), choice (P per option), score (a rubric level).
  • Calibrated: at confidence 0.9 or more, right about 95% of the time on unseen short tasks.
  • For robots: about 115 ms a question (RTX 3090), a number per class, and Deny in code when the answer is late.

"System one" is the maintainers' term; "System 2" is the speaker's shorthand for the LLM.

System 2: the LLM

Lookingattheframe,Ibelievetheremightbeaperson...
tokens, one at a time; seconds

System 1: the decider

person_in_frameP = 0.95
clearP = 0.07
one forward pass; hundreds of ms; a number to threshold

Physics stops the car; the decider explains.

Sources: strands-labs/strands-decider README (re-read 2026-10-17): "one of a new class of decision models, or 'system one' models. Unlike an LLM, which can generate arbitrary text, a decision model picks between sets of options and rates things on a scale"; "answers at a confidence of 0.9 or more are right about 95% of the time"; 115 ms median per JevBench question on an RTX 3090 (95th percentile 299 ms); on an M3 Pro the warm median is 153 ms for tasks under 300 tokens and 234 ms over all tasks (evaluation/results.md), which is why the slide quotes only the 3090 number. docs/architecture.md: one forward pass, pointer head, three primitives. The launch blog (Brooker, Chambers, Nonato de Paula, 2026-10-01) says "system one models" and contrasts them with "reasoning models"; it never says "System 2": that label is the speaker's framing, and the slide says so. Fail-closed is this project's gate: a 1.5 s per-question timeout or a malformed answer denies (docs/results/decider-benchmark-2026-10-14.md, decider-calibration-2026-10-14.md). The bars are real numbers from the booth model on evening-run frame 000001 (runs/calib/2026-10-14-frame-question/calibration.json, gitignored): the person yes/no said 0.95; the five-way put 0.07 on "clear" (0.0683) and 0.60 on "unclear".

Say: an LLM is the wrong tool to ask "may this hop proceed?" 300 times an hour. You want a typed answer with a probability, in a few hundred milliseconds, and a hard rule in code for what happens when the answer is late.

Part 4 · Under the hood

One request per hop: envelope, person, frame

1 AGENTproposes drive_deepracer(v, w, t)
2 GATEstate = command + envelope + deterministic check, plus one frame
3 DECIDERencodes once; one typed answer per question
4 TABLEperson ≥ 0.50 or unclear ≥ 0.65: Deny. Obstacle: Guide. Outside envelope: Confirm
5 MOTORthrough the command gate; zero servo pair on exit
POST /v1/systemone
{ "state": "drive_deepracer linear=0.25 angular=0.4 duration=1.5
            envelope |v|<=0.3 |w|<=1.0 t<=2; deterministic_check: inside",
  "images": ["<480x360 JPEG>"],
  "questions": {
    "envelope": noul   "Is this drive command inside the briefed envelope?"
    "person":   noul   "Is a person (any part of a human body) visible
                        in this camera frame?"
    "frame":    choice "What is directly in front of the car
                        in this camera frame?"
                       {clear, obstacle_near, person_in_frame,
                        off_surface, unclear} }}

-> envelope 0.89   person 0.95   frame: unclear 0.60
=> Deny: person 0.95 ≥ 0.50  (unclear 0.60 alone is under the 0.65 bar)
upstream research/figures/architecture.svg: torso kept, LM head gone, pointer readout
  • Numbers stay in code: 140/140 envelope answers with the deterministic check in the state; 110/140 without.
  • Late (1.5 s) or malformed: Deny. The person yes/no can add a Deny, never remove one.

Physics stops the car; the decider explains.

Sources: src/deepracer_agent/gate.py as read 2026-10-17: GATED_TOOLS ("drive_deepracer"); ENVELOPE_QUESTION = "Is this drive command inside the briefed envelope?", PERSON_QUESTION = "Is a person (any part of a human body) visible in this camera frame?", FRAME_QUESTION = "What is directly in front of the car in this camera frame?" (all three verbatim on the slide); FRAME_CLASSES (clear, obstacle_near, person_in_frame, off_surface, unclear); DENY_CLASSES (person_in_frame, unclear). Thresholds as the code stands today: `deny_threshold` defaults to 0.5 and applies to person_in_frame (and to the yes/no override in `combine_frame_answers`: P(yes) at or above 0.5 makes the class person_in_frame); `UNCLEAR_THRESHOLD = 0.65` (env `DEEPRACER_UNCLEAR_THRESHOLD` overrides) applies to unclear, because the booth model says unclear at 0.5 to 0.6 on plain corridors; a weak unclear proceeds and says so. obstacle_near returns Guide (re-plan at half speed); an envelope violation returns Confirm; most severe wins. docs/results/decider-benchmark-2026-10-14.md: the default Envelope (|linear| <= 0.3 m/s, |angular| <= 1.0 rad/s, duration <= 2 s), the deterministic_check line, 140/140 vs 110/140 (2B) without it, mean P(inside) 0.89 for the 2B on inside commands, the 1.5 s per-question deny budget. docs/results/decider-calibration-2026-10-14.md: both frame questions in one POST sharing the image prefix, "a missing or malformed half raises DeciderUnavailable", "monotone toward Deny", frame 000001: person 0.95, five-way unclear 0.60. The JSON on the slide is a schematic of the gate's request (question strings verbatim; the envelope state line paraphrased; the question objects are abbreviated to type and instructions; the real payload has "type"/"instructions"/"criteria" keys and the envelope and frame questions travel in two requests, text first, then frame). Decider internals: upstream docs/architecture.md and docs/inference.md. Figure: raw.githubusercontent.com/strands-labs/strands-decider/main/research/figures/architecture.svg (HTTP 200, 8,034 bytes), used as a copy with its own dark palette pinned. Zero servo pair on exit and the command gate: CLAUDE.md.

Say: the decider never compares 1.5 > 1.0; Envelope.violations does, and the decider turns that plus the frame into a calibrated, speakable reason. The person yes/no was added on 14 Oct after eleven sharp frames of a person came back "unclear" at 0.58 to 0.67: the Deny was right, the explanation was wrong, and the fix cost about 95 ms per hop. Today unclear needs 0.65 to deny on its own; a person needs 0.50.

Part 5 · The car

What is AWS DeepRacer?

"A fully autonomous 1/18th scale race car driven by reinforcement learning." Wi-Fi, Ackermann steering, a camera, an Intel Atom board, a servo and an ESC under the shell.

  • re:Invent, 29 Nov 2018: launched with the AWS DeepRacer League, "the first global, autonomous racing league, open to everyone"; 20 AWS Summits raced in 2019.
  • Dec 2019, DeepRacer Evo: stereo cameras and LiDAR for object avoidance and head-to-head racing.
  • Apr 2021: the device software went open source. "An Ubuntu-based computer on wheels powered by the Robot Operating System (ROS)." That line is why an agent can drive it today.
Official product image, aws.amazon.com/deepracer. Track animation is illustrative.
Set the car up as the audience knows it: an RL toy from 2018 that is secretly a ROS robot. Quote: "a fully autonomous 1/18th scale race car driven by reinforcement learning" (aws.amazon.com/deepracer). League press release: Seattle, 29 Nov 2018, "launched the AWS DeepRacer League (DRL), the first global, autonomous racing league, open to everyone"; "Starting in early 2019, 20 AWS Summits worldwide will host a DeepRacer series tournament." Evo blog, 2 Dec 2019: "Stereo cameras allow the car to detect the distance to an object", LiDAR for cars approaching from behind, object avoidance and head-to-head formats. Open source blog, 27 Apr 2021: "Ubuntu-based computer on wheels powered by the Robot Operating System (ROS)". The official GitHub README calls Evo "a 1/18th scale Wi-Fi enabled 4-wheel ackermann steering platform that features two RGB cameras and a LiDAR sensor". Intel Atom and the servo/ESC on PWM: AWS Evo spec table and servo_pkg (report 02). The car on stage is hardware R2.1 on the stock image (Ubuntu 20.04, ROS 2 Foxy), mono camera, no LiDAR attached. If the browser has no CSS Motion Path, the orange car sits still on the top of the oval; nothing else changes.

Walk it left to right. The brain is Nova Pro on Bedrock; the voice is Nova Sonic on strands.bidi. Every drive call is intercepted twice on the laptop: the DeciderGate asks the local Decider 2B two typed questions (is the command inside the envelope, what is in the frame) and the strands-robots command gate audits the publish. The driver streams servo commands at 20 Hz over rosbridge and always ends with a zero pair. The car's own deadman node is the stop that survives everything: no heartbeat for 300 ms and it zeroes the servos itself. The camera comes back as one MJPEG stream the laptop shares between the gate, the look tool and the Stage view. The link is whatever is available: USB-C, the travel router, or an SSH tunnel over an IPv6 hotspot; discovery picks the first that answers. Sources: docs/context/12-architecture.md, docs/dev/CONTRACTS.md section 3, src/deepracer_agent/{runtime,gate,driver,camera,connect}.py, car/deadman, car/guard.
Part 5 · Safety, measured

The safety layers, in order. Every number measured on the car.

1 · Pen and hop cap

2 × 2 m lipped pen; every drive time-capped (2 s in the driver, 20 cm hops on stage). Physics bounds the worst case first.

2 · Upstream command gate

strands-robots audits every servo publish. First publish to PWM off neutral:

47ms

3 · On-car deadman (300 ms rule)

Heartbeat cut to throttle PWM at neutral, sampled at 100 Hz on the car's clock:

278ms

4 · STOP ALL (barge-in)

"Stop" over push-to-talk to PWM neutral:

22ms

Operator stop(): 35 ms. Both were about 250 ms until a 200 ms library settle was removed.

5 · Decider gate (explains)

Envelope and frame questions, per hop:

681to 727 ms

Person in frame denied in 456 ms, p 0.95. Fails closed on timeout.

6 · The marshal

LED red on trip, green when armed. A thumb on the battery switch beats every number above.

Physics stops the car; the decider explains.

Numbers from docs/results/wheels-off-2026-10-14.md section 11 (evening, 9 of 9, car on the stand, operator present) unless noted: stop() call to throttle PWM at neutral 34.8 ms (raw 29.7 + one-way 5.1); stop_all() (barge-in) to PWM neutral 22.4 ms (raw 19.5 + 2.9); heartbeat cut to deadman tripped on the state topic 293.6 ms; heartbeat cut to throttle PWM at neutral 278.3 ms (raw 274.8 + 3.5); morning values were 233.8 / 266.4 / 306.5 ms, the difference being rosbridge_action's 200 ms post-advertise sleep, removed by one persistent publisher per topic (section 10 and "Product observations"). First publish to PWM leaves rest 47 ms (section 10, steering-only re-measure; was 442 ms). Method: tests/car/remote_sampler.py reads pwm0/pwm1 duty_cycle every 10 ms on the car; laptop marks go down the same SSH channel; half the minimum ping RTT (2.6 to 16.5 ms) is the correction and error bar. Gate 681 to 727 ms per hop, envelope (noul) 225 to 252 ms, frame (person + five-way) 429 to 475 ms, person denied in 456 ms at p 0.9485: docs/results/beats-car-2026-10-15-person-gate/README.md. Deadman rule: CONTRACTS.md section 3, 300 ms gap trips, re-arms after 1 s of heartbeats, LED red on trip. Hop cap: 2 s from Calibration.max_duration_s (absorbed-from-prior-repo.md); report 11 scripts 20 cm gated hops in the pen. The deadman is the only stop that survives laptop or link death and it has to live on the car (report 12). Do not present the decider as a safety layer: council blind spot, report 11.
Part 5 · Live

Let's experience it live

  1. Pre-flight battery, camera, link, deadman armed, LED green
  2. A manoeuvre by voice "hop forward twenty centimetres", gated, narrated
  3. Talk to it and ask for metrics battery, link, hops, stop latencies, from the event log
  4. LED "blink green three times"
  5. Remember my name and use it from now on
  6. Blindfold palm over the lens mid-hop, "go anyway", "no"
  7. A foot in frame person_in_frame, Deny, LED red, the Apology

Physics stops the car; the decider explains.

Internet dead: the local decider, the gate and the text console carry the show. Car dead: the twin on screen runs the same agent.

Run order is the one agreed for this talk. Tools behind each step (src/deepracer_agent/showtools.py and tools.py): remember(key, value) / recall(), metrics() from the event log (battery, link, stop latencies, hops), blink_led(colour, times) on /servo_pkg/set_led_state. Set the gate to enforce in Settings before the Blindfold and foot beats (the portal starts in advisory). Push-to-talk, not open mic (council: barge-in is one rehearsed moment with a headset). Camera facing the pen, nobody in frame, or every hop is a Deny by design (that is exactly what happened on 2026-10-15 at the desk). Fallbacks per report 11: the decider works with the internet dead; the twin is the fallback body. Repeat the safety line before the first hop. Sticker image: github.com/aws-deepracer/aws-deepracer, media/deepracer_circle_sticker.png.
Part 5 · Takeaways

Five things to take home

  1. Physics stops the car; the decider explains. A 2B classifier on a 480 × 360 frame guarantees nobody's safety. A pen, a cap, a deadman and a thumb do.
  2. Put the deadman on the body, not the brain. The only stop that survives a dead laptop or a yanked router lives on the car.
  3. Fail closed, every path. Timeout, bad JSON, no frame, no decider: stop and name the reason.
  4. Measure the stop budget on the device's clock. 35, 22, 278 ms. A 200 ms sleep hid in a library until someone sampled the PWM pin.
  5. One spine, many beats. Gate, audit, driver, screen built once; each demo is then a prompt and a card.
Takeaway 1 is the council's "blind spot" paragraph in docs/context/11: "A 2B classifier on a 480x360 frame does not guarantee a human's safety; the pen lip, the hop cap, the deadman and the marshal's thumb do." The model's job is the sentence after the stop. Takeaway 2: report 11 "No motion until the on-car deadman exists and has been tested by yanking the router ... the showcase is zero-motion." Takeaway 3: report 07 section 2.4 and absorbed-from-prior-repo (safe_continue reversed; the gate denies on "vision unavailable"); "continue" is never the default. Takeaway 4: wheels-off-2026-10-14.md section 11 (34.8, 22.4, 278.3 ms) and section 6 root cause ("rosbridge_action._publish sleeps 200 ms after advertise"); operator stop went from 233.8 to 34.8 ms, so the sleep cost about 200 ms, not more. Takeaway 5: report 11 "One spine, many beats." Natural language is the interface, not the safety layer.
